name: Colorado (COMPS Order #39, YEOA, HFWA)

overtime.note: COMPS Rule 4.1.1: over 40/workweek, over 12/workday, or over 12 consecutive hours regardless of the workday, whichever gives the greater pay, without duplication.

meal.note: Uninterrupted, duty-free 30-minute meal period when a shift exceeds 5 hours; otherwise an on-duty paid meal.

rest.note: 10 paid minutes per 4 hours or major fraction; a required rest period not authorized/permitted is owed as extra pay (COMPS 5.2.4).

ages.note: Not yet verified: Colorado Youth Employment Opportunity Act limits (8 h/day, 40 h/week for minors); school-day limits may be stricter.

minimumWage.youthDiscountNote: Unemancipated minors may be paid up to 15% below the state minimum, but not where a local minimum wage applies.

sickLeave.law: Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act
sickLeave.note: HFWA: 1 hour paid sick leave per 30 hours worked, up to 48 hours per year; up to 48 unused hours carry over. Not yet verified against the official source.

involuntary.note: C.R.S. 8-4-109: wages are due immediately when the employer ends the employment (with short extensions when the accounting unit is closed or offsite). Not yet verified against the official source.

voluntary.note: C.R.S. 8-4-109: when the employee quits, wages are due by the next regular payday. Not yet verified against the official source.

ptoPayout.note: Colorado: earned, unused vacation is wages and is paid at separation (Nieto v. Clark's Market, 2021); paid sick leave under HFWA is not. Not yet verified against the official source.

leave.note: Colorado FAMLI: up to 12 weeks of paid family and medical leave (more in some pregnancy cases), paid by the state program; job protection after 180 days of employment. Not yet verified against the official source.
Healthy Families and Workplaces Act paid sick leave; tracked as a time-off policy, protected (never counts against attendance).
